tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Interior interpolation inequality] 1. ch6:6.32\group gt-ch06 If $j+\beta <k+\alpha $, $u\in C^{k,\alpha }(\Omega )$, and $\Omega $ is open, then for every $\varepsilon >0$, \begin{equation} \tag {6.82} [u]^*_{j,\beta ;\Omega }\le C(\varepsilon )|u|_{0;\Omega }+\varepsilon [u]^*_{k,\alpha ;\Omega }, \end{equation} and \[ |u|^*_{j,\beta ;\Omega }\le C(\varepsilon )|u|_{0;\Omega }+\varepsilon [u]^*_{k,\alpha ;\Omega }. \]
Proof

\sketch The base case $j=1$, $k=2$, $\alpha =\beta =0$ is

\begin{equation} \tag {6.83} [u]^*_1\leq C(\varepsilon )|u|_0+\varepsilon [u]^*_2. \end{equation}

For $d=\mu d_x$, use finite differences on $B_d(x)$ when the two points are close and the trivial $2|u|_0$ bound otherwise. Apply the mean-value theorem to derivatives and choose $\mu $ so the high-order seminorm coefficient is at most $\varepsilon $. The cases $\alpha =0$ or $\beta =0$ follow by induction on the derivative order.

□
